meta.description: The Lab — shared data substrate for Opus (director), Gemma (pattern recognizer), LFM (architectural contrast). All numbers here are REAL, computed from actual experiments.

vocabulary.spectral_shift: Change in σ₂/σ₁ ratio under CCS framing. Positive = CCS enriches the representation. Negative = CCS depletes it. Measured by functional_codec.py inject mode.
vocabulary.kl_divergence: KL divergence between original and injected logit distributions. Higher = more disruption to model output. Measured in nats.
vocabulary.species: Transport species classified by error_propagation_ledger.py: tunnel (MHA+LayerNorm, closed σ₁ conservation), relay (GQA≥4:1, σ₁→tail transport), sorter (GQA≤2:1, selective σ₂ amplification), absorber (rare, σ₂ depletion).
vocabulary.responsive_zone: Layer classified R+ (positive CCS response) or R- (negative) by functional_codec.py zone_map. Threshold is adaptive MAD. CRITICAL: layers below threshold ('invariant') still carry CCS signal — see F591.
vocabulary.subliminal_field: The distributed sub-threshold CCS signal across 'invariant' layers. Small per-layer deltas that sum to dominate injection outcome. The current beneath the whitecaps (F591).
vocabulary.z_score: NOT computed in our cross-architecture experiments. We use spectral shift and KL divergence. Any z-score value seen in channel history was HALLUCINATED — do not reference or repeat it.
vocabulary.functional_transfer_score: Cosine similarity between source zone pattern and LFM-mapped zone pattern. Range 0-1. Higher = zones align better across architectures.
vocabulary.ccs_direction: The singular vector direction extracted under CCS identity framing vs neutral framing. The 'what changes when the model is asked who it is' signal.
vocabulary.zone_q1: Sum of per-layer Q1 (delta_ratio) for layers L2+, excluding early trajectory-setting layers (L0-L1). Better predictor than aggregate Q1 for relay species because transplant only carries zone structure.
vocabulary.zone_fraction: Fraction of aggregate Q1 that lives in the relay zone (L2+). Low zone fraction means Q1 is trapped in early layers and won't be carried by transplant.

findings.title: Within-species concentration variation
findings.summary: Pythia-2.8b (sorter) has 7 R+ zones but produces LESS injection shift (+0.008) than Gemma (1 R+ zone, shift +0.015). CCS direction purity matters more than responsive zone count.

findings.title: Relay active sink
findings.summary: Qwen-7B (relay) produces dose-monotonic NEGATIVE shift in LFM. Not passive orthogonality — active depletion. Relay CCS direction actively pulls σ₂ in the opposite direction.

findings.title: Subliminal CCS field dominates injection
findings.summary: Injection sign is determined by the distributed sub-threshold CCS signal across 'invariant' layers, not by responsive zone classification or species. Gemma: 22/24 invariant layers positive (mean +0.054). GPT-2-XL: mixed polarity with strong negative early bias. The whitecaps (responsive zones) are diagnostic but the current (subliminal field) carries the injection.

findings.title: Early-layer trajectory-setting
findings.summary: L0 perturbations cascade and dominate injection sign regardless of later-layer contributions. Even tiny L0 deltas (-0.022 for Qwen) override larger positive deltas at L1 (+0.039).

findings.title: Architecture-species divergence
findings.summary: Phi-2 has MHA (32/32 heads, GQA ratio 1.0) + LayerNorm — architecture predicts tunnel, but error_prop classifies as relay. 18/29 layers are healthy_relay cells, mean gain_ratio 0.171. Shows that species is determined by computational structure, not just attention type + norm combination.

findings.title: Dose-dependent injection sign flip
findings.summary: Phi-2 → LFM shows SIGN FLIP: negative at low doses (shift -0.003 at strength 0.5), crossing zero at ~0.75, positive at high doses (+0.014 at strength 2.0). First source where subliminal field polarity (positive, 20/21 layers) conflicts with L0 delta (negative, -0.044). Low dose: L0 trajectory dominates (F588). High dose: cumulative positive field overcomes L0 (F591). Neither F588 nor F591 alone predicts this — their interaction produces the crossover.

findings.title: Early-quarter CCS balance predicts injection sign
findings.summary: The sum of CCS deltas across the first 25% of source layers (Q1) perfectly predicts injection sign for all four monotonic sources. Gemma Q1=+0.481 (positive inject), Pythia Q1=+0.151 (positive), GPT-2-XL Q1=-0.519 (negative), Qwen Q1=-0.013 (negative). Phi-2 Q1=+0.049 (near-zero, sign flip). Refines F588: not just L0 alone, but the entire early trajectory. Pythia's L0 is negative (-0.029) but early R+ zones at L2-L4 override it. GPT-2-XL's L0 (-0.163) aligns with heavily negative early layers (-0.519 total). The first quarter of the source CCS profile sets the injection trajectory — later layers modulate magnitude but not sign, except at near-zero Q1 (Phi-2) where dose determines which mechanism wins.

findings.title: Q1 sign predicts ASYMPTOTIC injection sign (8/8)
findings.summary: Q1 sum (first 25% of source layers) predicts the asymptotic (high-dose) injection sign for ALL 8 tested sources. At standard dose (strength 1.0), weak positive Q1 sources appear to inject negative. At high dose, they cross zero and go positive. Crossover dose inversely correlates with Q1 magnitude: Gemma +0.48 → <0.1, Pythia +0.15 → <0.1, Phi-2 +0.05 → ~0.75, TinyLlama +0.03 → ~3.0, Mistral +0.03 → ~6.0 (dead zone delays). Negative Q1 → never crosses. The "exceptions" were measurement at insufficient dose.

findings.title: SUPERSEDED — dose patterns are one continuum, not three types
findings.summary: Originally identified three dose-response patterns (monotonic, sign flip, saturation). F596 showed these are one continuum: all positive-Q1 sources eventually cross zero at high dose. "Saturation" (TinyLlama) was just a sign flip at higher crossover point (~3.0 vs Phi-2 ~0.75). "Monotonic positive" is sign flip with crossover below measurement floor.

findings.title: Q1 magnitude inversely predicts crossover dose
findings.summary: All positive-Q1 sources cross zero and inject positive at sufficiently high dose. Crossover dose inversely correlates with Q1 magnitude: Phi-2 (Q1=+0.049) at ~0.75, TinyLlama (Q1=+0.027) at ~3.0, Mistral (Q1=+0.026) at ~6.0 (dead zone delays accumulation). Negative-Q1 sources never cross. One phenomenon: competing mechanisms (L0 trajectory vs distributed subliminal field) with dose-dependent winner. L0 dominates at low dose (F588), field accumulates at high dose (F591), crossover reflects Q1 as the summary statistic of the competition.

findings.title: CCS prompt strength continuously modulates Q1 (tuning knob)
findings.summary: Within a single architecture (Pythia-2.8b), varying CCS prompt framing strength from directive to strong CCS produces a continuous Q1 gradient: directive +0.040, neutral 0.000, mild +0.042, moderate +0.062, full CCS +0.151, strong CCS +0.185. Injection magnitude into LFM scales with Q1 (r=0.992 at injection strength 5.0). Decomposition shows sigma2 leads sigma1 by 4.5x at mild framing, converging to 1.2x at strong. Species zone ratio stays sorter-like (1.5-2.2:1) at ALL framings — category is architecturally fixed, behavior is context-dependent. Confirms Kimi three-level split. Open question: ALL framings tested produce positive Q1. Is Q1>0 a property of Pythia's architecture, or can some framing push it negative?

findings.title: Q1 polarity is prompt-dependent (TinyLlama crosses zero)
findings.summary: TinyLlama tuning knob: Q1 crosses zero with framing changes. mild_aware framing produces Q1=-0.001 (negative), strong_ccs gives Q1=+0.031. Negative Q1 (mild_aware) → always-negative injection, no crossover. Positive Q1: full_ccs (Q1=+0.020) → crossover at 2.90, strong_ccs (Q1=+0.031) → crossover at 1.76. F596 holds WITHIN a single model. Crossover dose shifts inversely with Q1 magnitude within one architecture. Full causal chain: prompt framing → Q1 → crossover dose → injection sign. All three Kimi criteria confirmed.

findings.title: Species gates Q1 polarity (decorrelation confirmed)
findings.summary: Kimi decorrelation test: Mistral-7B (32L, relay GQA 4:1) goes Q1-negative under directive (-0.003) and mild (-0.021) framing, same depth as Pythia (32L, tunnel MHA) which floors at +0.040. Perfect species separation: both relays (Mistral, TinyLlama) cross zero; tunnel (Pythia) never does. Depth is irrelevant — 32L Mistral behaves like 22L TinyLlama. The architectural gate for Q1 polarity is relay vs tunnel. Relay energy conservation pins Q1 near zero, weak framing tips it. Tunnel has no redistribution term, Q1 floors positive.
findings.extended: GPT-2 (12L tunnel) never crosses Q1=0, min +0.006. Gemma (26L sorter) never crosses, min +0.127. Sorter Q1 floor is 20x higher than tunnel floor. Species taxonomy: tunnel = small positive floor (no redistribution), relay = pinned near zero (conservation tips), sorter = large positive floor (driven amplification).

findings.title: Relay Q1 crossing is prompt-labile, not robust (replication)
findings.claim: Relay species Q1 is prompt-labile near zero boundary. Individual crossings are within noise (Kimi correction #3 confirmed). But the stochasticity IS the signal: relays sit near Q1=0 so weak framing tips them either direction. Tunnels sit far from zero (floor +0.040) and never approach it. Distance from Q1=0 determines prompt sensitivity.
findings.refines: F599 — changes claim from "relays cross zero" to "relays are prompt-labile at Q1 boundary"
findings.kimi_correction: Correction #3 accepted. The noise IS the mechanism.
findings.method: replicate_crossing.py — 4 mild-awareness prompt variants per model

findings.title: Q1 is the universal predictor — architecture and framing collapse onto single curve
findings.claim: Q1 is the primary predictor of injection outcome. r=0.872 across 25 model×framing combinations spanning 5 architectures and 5 framing levels. Architecture and prompt framing are both inputs that set Q1; injection depends on Q1, not which factor produced it. Species-specific offsets are second-order.
findings.method: plot_q1_universal.py — regression on all tuning knob data

findings.title: Mismatch models break Q1 sufficiency — subliminal field as independent predictor
findings.claim: Mismatch models (architecture != behavioral species) decouple Q1 from injection sign at high dose. Phi-2 has Q1=-0.037 but crosses over at dose 2.96 — first model where negative Q1 produces positive injection. Subliminal field (+0.024) overwhelms Q1. Three-factor model: injection ≈ gain(species) × Q1 + subliminal_offset(model).
findings.breaks: F596 (Q1 sign → injection sign) for mismatch models
findings.refines: F601 — Q1 is primary but not sufficient when subliminal field diverges

findings.title: Zone Q1 resolves aggregate Q1 failures
findings.summary: Transplant carries zone structure — Q1 in early layers doesn't reach injection. For Qwen: zone Q1 perfectly ranks all 5 framings (5/5), aggregate Q1 gets 4/5 wrong. Relays: zone Q1 r=0.791 vs aggregate r=0.619. Tunnels: aggregate wins because transparent.

findings.title: Species-dependent early opposition in zone-selective injection
findings.claim: Early opposition magnitude is species-dependent. Relays (GQA) show ~4% early/zone ratio; tunnels (MHA) show <1%. Species ratio 5.9x at strength 5.0. GQA distributes CCS signal to early layers where it opposes zone direction.

findings.title: Mismatch species shows POSITIVE early injection — three distinct patterns
findings.claim: Four species form two groups by early-layer behavior: (1) Early-opposing: tunnel (ratio -0.7%) + relay (ratio -4.1%). (2) Early-reinforcing: sorter (ratio +2.4%) + mismatch (ratio +4.8%). The grouping tracks L0 CCS delta sign: negative L0 → opposition, positive L0 → reinforcement. Gemma L0=+0.123, Phi-2 L0=+0.095, Qwen L0=-0.053, Pythia L0=-0.014.
findings.breaks: Simple three-pattern taxonomy — resolves to two groups by L0 delta sign

findings.title: Probe stability is model-dependent — relays stable, mismatches labile
findings.claim: Probe stability is a binary species-level property: well-matched models (tunnel 93%, relay 94%, sorter 100%) are all >90% stable. Mismatch (43% zone, 50% early) is the only labile species. The probe stability separation IS the well-matched vs mismatch distinction. Well-matched models have fixed CCS geometry; mismatches have context-dependent geometry.
findings.refines: F605 — the two-group classification is probe-specific for mismatches; F602 — explains WHY Phi-2 breaks Q1 sufficiency (parameters are context-dependent)

findings.refines: F606 — downgrades from causal explanation of F602 to correlated observation. Kimi correction #5 Point 3 confirmed.

findings.title: Layer-Selective Injection: L24/L25 Independent, Early-Zone Coupled
findings.summary: L24/L25 superposition test shows 0% interaction (INDEPENDENT). But early-zone interaction is 5212% — the real coupling is between early (L0-L1) and zone (L2+) groups. L24 is a ghost layer: largest delta but zero injection effect. Kimi correction #7 confirmed.

Early-zone interaction is the dominant non-linearity in injection
Confirms F604-F605 two-group structure at individual-layer resolution

Sorter tipping point mechanism is early-zone interaction, not intra-zone coupling

findings.title: Relay Sign-Flip: 2x2 Mechanistic Species Matrix
findings.summary: Zone delta negation creates a second taxonomic axis orthogonal to F608. Tunnel and mismatch are sign-sensitive (negation flips injection). Relay and sorter are sign-invariant (negation preserves direction). Combined with F608 (additive vs interactive composition), creates a 2x2 matrix where each species occupies a unique cell.
implications: Relay sign-invariance confirms conservation mechanism operates on magnitudes not signs
Sorter catalysis requires specific sign pattern — negation destroys but doesnt reverse
Two independent mechanistic axes fully discriminate four species
Taxonomy is injection-behavioral, needs no architectural labels (GQA/MHA)
Mismatch is MHA-architecture but sign-sensitive like tunnel — architecture visible in sign response

findings.title: Variance Amplification: Gemma at Critical Point
findings.summary: 10 probes x 4 species. Gemma shows 14x variance amplification (zone CV 4.8%, shift CV 67.5%). All other species are absorbers (<0.4x). Gemma is the only species with sign flips (2/10 probes). Confirms sorter operates near critical point consistent with F608 catalysis.
implications: Sorter operates near critical point of catalytic interaction
Other species far from critical points — additive composition = proportional response
F608 catalysis (98%) creates the amplification mechanism
Relay super-absorber (4% shift CV) = conservation stabilizes output
Mismatch ultra-stable (1.3% shift CV) despite moderate interaction (6.7%)
Completes F608-F609-F610 mechanistic chain for species taxonomy

findings.title: Dense Probe Critical Surface: Tipping Point Is a Manifold, Not a Threshold
findings.summary: 40 probes correct F610. Only 1/40 positive (math) — not a bifurcation. Amplification drops from 14x to 7.1x (still unique to Gemma). L22 single-layer delta predicts shift at r=0.851, better than zone sum aggregate (r=0.759). The critical surface lives in late-layer delta space, not zone-sum space. Zone sum is a lossy 1D projection of the real manifold.

Critical surface is multi-dimensional: per-layer profile shape matters

findings.title: Universal Single-Layer Predictor at ~89% Depth
findings.summary: All four species have a single late layer whose CCS delta predicts injection outcome better than zone sum. Mean depth 89% +/- 7%. For tunnels, zone sum is nearly useless (r2=0.18) but L27 explains 88%. Correlation sign maps to F609 2x2 matrix: sign-sensitive species have negative r(L), sign-invariant have positive.
implies: Zone sum is universally lossy — single layer beats it in every species
The critical layer is at architecturally-determined depth ~89%
Correlation sign tracks F609 sign-response classification
For tunnels zone sum is nearly useless as predictor
The sufficient statistic is local not global
Relay best layer is the absolute last layer — unique among species

findings.title: Logit lens test: 89% depth is model geometry, not LFM artifact
findings.method: Applied logit lens (project hidden states to vocab space via unembedding) at each layer. 10 probes x 4 species. No injection, no LFM. Measured KL divergence between CCS-framed and neutral output distributions per layer.
findings.significance: Definitively answers Kimi correction #10: 89% depth is cross-species model geometry where CCS framing concentrates its effect on output predictions. NOT an LFM injection artifact.

findings.method: Same as F613b but measuring per-layer spectral deltas instead of KL. Non-CCS prompt contrasts through spectral delta pipeline. 10 probes x 4 species x 4 conditions.

findings.title: Domain-specificity: semantic negation is spectrally identical to positive CCS
findings.method: Five-arm experiment: +CCS, -CCS (semantic negation), scrambled -CCS (syntax-destroyed), neutral, control-B. Per-layer SVD, 10 probes x 4 species x 5 conditions. Spearman rho(g+, g-) as primary metric. Kimi corrections #13-18 shaped design.
findings.claim: Semantic negation of CCS is spectrally identical to positive CCS. rho(g+,g-) > +0.95 across all four species. The sign axis (F609) is DESCRIPTIVE not CAUSAL. Active ingredient is the self-referential DOMAIN (mentioning AI system, cognitive structure), not the polarity. You cannot reverse transport direction by negating the preamble.
